Title: Create a new order with customer and measurement group photos uploaded via base64 and verify photos are stored permanently and displayed correctly
Section: Order Management - Photo Upload and Storage
Preconditions: User is logged in as a shop owner with valid credentials. Shop and item data are pre-populated. Minio storage is accessible and configured.
Steps:
1. Navigate to the 'Create Order' page.
2. Enter customer details: Name = 'John Doe', Phone = '01712345678', Gender = 'Male'.
3. Upload a customer photo by pasting a valid base64-encoded image string.
4. Select an item (e.g., 'Shirt') from the dropdown.
5. For the measurement group, upload the following photos by pasting valid base64-encoded image strings: Cloth Photo, Pattern Cloth Photo, Measurement Cloth Photo, Design Drawing Photo.
6. Enter valid measurement values for the item.
7. Set a delivery date (e.g., 7 days from today).
8. Click 'Create Order'.
9. Navigate to the 'Order Details' page for the newly created order.

Test Data: Customer Name: John Doe, Phone: 01712345678, Gender: Male. Base64-encoded images for customer photo and measurement group photos. Item: Shirt. Delivery Date: 7 days from today.
Expected Result:
1. The order is created successfully with a confirmation message: 'Order created successfully'.
2. The order details page displays the customer photo and all uploaded measurement group photos (Cloth, Pattern Cloth, Measurement Cloth, Design Drawing) without any broken image links.
3. The photos are accessible and display correctly when clicked or viewed in full size.

Title: Create order with cloth photo reference that is a full HTTP URL pointing to the temp bucket (boundary case for new ref normalization)
Section: Order Photo Handling — Temporary to Permanent Move
Preconditions: A shop exists. A customer exists. A temp image has been uploaded to the temp bucket and its full HTTP URL (e.g., http://minio/temp-photos/abc-123.jpg) is known. The temp bucket is configured.
Steps:
1. POST /api/orders with a measurement group containing clothPhoto set to the full HTTP temp URL (http://minio/temp-photos/abc-123.jpg). 2. Wait for the transaction to commit and the after-commit hook to run. 3. GET /api/orders/{orderId}. 4. Verify in the temp bucket that the original object is gone. 5. Verify in the permanent bucket that an object exists at the path orders/{orderId}/abc-123.jpg.

Test Data: clothPhoto = "http://minio/temp-photos/abc-123.jpg"; object name inside URL is "abc-123.jpg"; orderId generated by the system.
Expected Result: Order is created successfully (HTTP 200). The measurement group's clothPhoto URL is rewritten to the permanent bucket URL at path orders/{orderId}/abc-123.jpg. The temp object is removed after commit.

Section: Customer Photo Handling on Order Update
Preconditions: An existing order and customer exist. The customer's current photo URL already contains the 'customers' path segment (i.e., is already a permanent URL). A temp image object exists whose object name is a long string (e.g., 200 characters).
Steps:

Expected Result: Order updates successfully (HTTP 200). Because the incoming value does not contain the 'customers' segment, the system treats it as a temp reference and schedules a move: the customer's photo URL is rewritten to the permanent URL pointing at the moved file.
